mynaya: Minaya — spelling of Minaya with y (see minaya), the title by which the Cid's kinsman Álvar Fáñez is called
daquestos: de + aquestos — of these (preposition de + aquestos, masc. pl. of the reinforced demonstrative aqueste; daquestos moros 'of these Moors'; = de estos)
tajador: tajador — cutting, sharp (adjective, from tajar 'to cut'; espada tajador 'a cutting sword'; = cortante)
sangriento: sangriento — bloody, blood-stained (masc. sg.; sangriento trae el braço 'he carries his arm bloody'; = sangriento)
dize: dezir — he says (present 3rd sg.; Dize Minaya 'Minaya says'; = dice)
lid: lid — battle, fight (fem. noun; lid campal 'pitched battle'; vençiemos la lid 'we won the battle'; = lid, now literary, closest batalla, combate)
campal: campal — of the field, pitched (adjective, from campo; lid campal 'a battle in the open field'; = campal)
yazen: yazer — they lie (present 3rd pl.; yazen muertos 'they lie dead'; = yacen)
dexados: dexar — left (past part. masc. pl., agreeing with the object after a 'has'; pocos bivos a dexados 'he has left few alive'; = dejados)
andava: andar — he was going, was riding (imperfect 3rd sg.; Andava mio Çid sobre so buen cavallo 'the Cid was riding on his good horse'; = andaba)
cofia: cofia — coif, the close cap worn under the helmet or hood of mail (cofia fronzida 'the coif wrinkled/gathered'; = cofia)
fronzida: fronzir — gathered, drawn up in folds (past part. fem., agreeing with cofia; la cofia fronzida, Pidal 'fruncida sobre la cara', the coif drawn up about the face; = fruncida)
barbado: barbado — bearded, having a full beard (adjective from barba; cómmo es bien barbado 'how well bearded he is'; = barbado)
almófar: almófar — hood of mail worn over the head and neck (word of Arabic origin; almófar a cuestas 'the mail hood thrown back on the shoulders'; = almófar)
cuestas: cuesta — back, shoulders (fem. pl. here; a cuestas 'on the back', with the hood hanging behind; modern cuesta usually 'slope'; = a cuestas)
commos: commo + se — how … (themselves) (commo 'how' + reflexive se cut to s; commos van allegando 'how they come gathering'; = cómo se)
allegando: allegar — gathering, coming together, drawing near (gerund; se van allegando 'they come gathering, assembling'; = allegándose, juntándose)
albergada: albergada — encampment, camp (noun from albergar 'to lodge'; Pidal 'campamento'; esta albergada 'this camp'; = campamento)
robado: robar — plundered, stripped (past part.; la an robado 'they have plundered it'; = robado)
largos: largo — abundant, ample, generous (masc. pl.; averes largos 'plentiful goods'; = largos)
moriscos: morisco — Moorish (adjective, masc. pl.; used without its noun: de los moriscos 'of the Moorish ones', i.e. the Moors' horses; = moriscos)
llegados: llegar — arrived, come (past part. masc. pl. after the auxiliary seer; quando son llegados 'when they have come'; = llegados)
ffallaron: fallar — they found (preterite 3rd pl.; ff- is a scribal spelling of initial f-, in medieval hands often standing for capital F; = hallaron)
alegreya: alegreya — joy, gladness (noun; grand alegreya 'great joy'; = alegría)
fallaron: fallar — they found (preterite 3rd pl.; = hallaron); fallar menos 'to find missing, to miss', Pidal 'echar de menos' (menos non fallaron 'they did not miss')
avién: aver — they had (imperfect 3rd pl., perfect auxiliary forming the pluperfect; que y avién fallado 'that they had found there'; = habían)
fallado: fallar — found (past part.; avién fallado 'they had found'; = hallado)
tornados: tornar — turned back, returned (past part. masc. pl., agreeing with los 'them'; a los moros dentro los an tornados 'they have put the Moors back inside'; = vueltos, devueltos)
dineros: dinero — money, coin (masc. pl.; estos dineros 'this money'; = dineros)
caen: caer — they fall (to), come as one's share (present 3rd pl.; al Çid caen cient cavallos 'a hundred horses fall to the Cid'; = caen)
cient: cient — hundred (apocopated before a noun; cient cavallos 'a hundred horses'; = cien)
pagó: pagar — he paid, rewarded (preterite 3rd sg.; qué bien pagó a todos sus vassallos 'how well he paid all his vassals'; = pagó)
encavalgados: encavalgado — mounted man, horseman (past part. used as a noun, masc. pl., opposed to peones 'foot-soldiers'; = encabalgados)
aguisa: aguisar — he arranges, sees to, provides for (present 3rd sg.; bien lo aguisa 'he arranges it well'; = dispone, prepara; aguisar is now obsolete)
riqueza: riqueza — wealth, riches (fem. sg.; D'aquesta riqueza 'of this wealth'; = riqueza)
desta: de + esta — of this (preposition de + demonstrative fem. sg.; desta batalla 'of this battle'; = de esta)
quiérol: quiero + le — I want to him (querer 1st sg. present + dative pronoun le with e elided after the verb; quiérol enbiar 'I want to send him'; = le quiero)
enfrenados: enfrenar — bridled, fitted with a bridle (past part. masc. pl., agreeing with cavallos; muy bien enfrenados 'very well bridled'; = enfrenados)
colgando: colgar — hanging (gerund; espadas … colgando 'swords hanging'; = colgando)
fina: fino — fine, pure (fem. sg., agreeing with plata; plata fina 'fine silver'; = fina)
uesa: uesa — high boot (Pidal's gloss 'bota alta', a boot used as a sack for small objects when clothes had no pockets; una uesa lleña 'a boot full'; = huesa, obsolete in this sense)
lleña: lleña — full (fem. sg., agreeing with uesa; una uesa lleña 'a boot full'; = llena; the -ñ- is a spelling variant)
mingua: minguar — it lacks, is wanting (present 3rd sg.; que nada nol mingua 'so that nothing is wanting to it'; = menguar, whence mengua 'lack')
quitedes: quitar — you pay (for), discharge (present subjunctive 2nd pl. used as a command, old -edes ending; quitedes mill missas 'have a thousand Masses paid for'; Pidal glosses 'paguéis')
romaneçiere: romaneçer — (if) it remains over (future subjunctive 3rd sg., -iere; Pidal: romanecer and remanecer, 'quedar, sobrar'; lo que romaneçiere 'whatever remains over'; = sobrare)
daldo: dad + lo — give it (imperative 2nd pl. dad with object lo, the d and l reversed: dadlo > daldo, metathesis; daldo a mi mugier 'give it to my wife'; = dadlo)
rueguen: rogar — let them pray, may they pray (present subjunctive 3rd pl., after que of wish; que rueguen por mí 'may they pray for me'; = rueguen)
noches: noche — night (fem. pl.; las noches e los días 'nights and days'; = noches)
contados: contar — counted, picked out (past part. masc. pl. with the auxiliary seer; por ir con él omnes son contados 'men are counted off to go with him'; = contados)
acordando: acordar — taking counsel (gerund; se acordando con los sos 'taking counsel with his men', the reflexive se before the gerund; = acordándose; cf. tornós a acordar)
nuestros: nuestro — our (masc. pl.; nuestros amigos 'our friends'; = nuestros)
podedes: poder — you can (present 2nd pl., old -edes ending; bien les podedes dezir 'you may well tell them'; = podéis)
valió: valer — he helped, aided (preterite 3rd sg.; Dios nos valió 'God helped us'; = valió)
vençiemos: vençer — we won (preterite 1st pl. with the ending -iemos; vençiemos la lid 'we won the battle'; = vencimos)
falláredes: fallar — (if) you find (future subjunctive 2nd pl., -áredes, not an indicative; si nos falláredes aquí 'if you find us here'; = hallareis)
sopiéredes: saber — (wherever) you learn, may learn (future subjunctive 2nd pl., on the strong preterite stem sop- of sope, sopo; do sopiéredes que somos 'wherever you learn that we are'; = supiereis)
indos: id + nos — go … us (imperative 2nd pl. id with the object pronoun nos, d and n transposed, idnos > indos, as dadlo > daldo; the nos is the object of the following infinitive: indos conseguir 'go and overtake us'; = id a alcanzarnos)
conseguir: conseguir — to follow, catch up with (infinitive; indos conseguir 'go and catch up with us'; modern conseguir means 'to obtain', closest alcanzar)
guarir: guarir — to save oneself, find safety, survive, get one's living (infinitive; avemos de guarir 'we must save ourselves, live'; = guarecerse)
angosta: angosto — narrow, scant, wretched (fem. sg., agreeing with tierra; tierra angosta 'a narrow, poor land'; = angosta, closest estrecha)
bivir: bivir — to live (infinitive; non podriemos bivir 'we could not live'; = vivir)
cuedo: cuedar — I think, suppose (present 1st sg.; old form of cuidar in its old sense 'to think'; commo yo cuedo 'as I think'; = creo, pienso)
avremos: aver — we shall have (future 1st pl., syncopated; a ir nos avremos 'we shall have to go', aver a + inf. with the clitic nos set inside the phrase; = habremos)

__broaden__.menos: menos — least, less · menos fallar — to find missing, to miss (de los sos menos non fallaron 'of their own men they missed no more than fifteen')
__broaden__.si: si — if; si + subjunctive alone = 'if only …!' · si non — otherwise, if not (si non, do sopiéredes 'if not, wherever you learn'); si + future subjunctive 'if' (si nos falláredes 'if you find us')
__broaden__.guisa: guisa — manner, fashion; a guisa de 'in the fashion of' · a vuestra guisa 'as you see fit, in your own way' (prended a vuestra guisa 'take as you please')
__broaden__.dio: dar — he gave, struck (preterite 3rd sg.; un colpe dio 'he struck a blow'; = dio) · dar a + inf. 'to give (something) to be …-ed' (Dio a partir estos dineros 'he had this money shared out')
__broaden__.tornada: tornada — turn, return, wheeling back (noun, from tornar; a la tornada 'on the return (charge)'; = vuelta) · a la tornada 'on (your) return' from a journey (A la tornada, si nos falláredes aquí 'on your return, if you find us here')
__broaden__.recabdo: recabdo — care, precaution, strict order (= recaudo) · also recabdo — business secured, a sure outcome (con todo buen recabdo 'with everything well in hand') · recabdo — account, reckoning (oro e plata que non saben recabdo 'gold and silver past all reckoning')
